discovery: Theory of quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computation
subfield: Quantum information physics / quantum error correction
motivation: In 1995-1997 Shor and Steane showed, against widespread doubt, that quantum information can be protected from decoherence without measuring it: redundant encoding and syndrome measurement can undo errors on continuous quantum states. Kitaev then showed how to store quantum information non-locally in the topology of a many-body system with his toric (surface) code, and helped establish the threshold theorem: below a critical error rate, arbitrarily long quantum computations become possible. These ideas turned decoherence from a fundamental barrier into an engineering problem. They have changed how we understand entanglement and many-body physics, and they now guide experiments worldwide. Recent superconducting and atomic experiments have shown logical qubits whose errors fall exponentially as code distance grows below threshold, which confirms the physical predictions of this theory. It is a basic insight that has become concrete and laid the foundation of a new technology.
